surveys.title: Newer Volcanic Province 2019
surveys.description: This collection comprises 54 broadband magnetotelluric (MT) sites acquired across the Newer Volcanic Province in South Australia and Victoria, in August 2019. Sites were deployed in a regular grid at roughly 25 km spacing to infill and enhance existing AusLAMP and state-based coverage, sharpening constraints on the three-dimensional lithospheric electrical structure beneath the province.

surveys.title: Vulcan 2024-25
surveys.description: A broadband magnetotelluric survey was conducted over the 2024 and 2025 field seasons to extend the Vulcan 2022 grid to the north-east, across the Vulcan iron oxide copper-gold (IOCG) prospect on the Stuart Shelf, in the Olympic Cu-Au Province of South Australia. The survey adds 20 MT stations at a nominal 2 km spacing, complementing the approximately 1 km grid of the 2022 survey and enlarging the imaged footprint of the electrical resistivity structure beneath the sedimentary cover of the prospect area; the extension ties directly into the 2022 stations so the two surveys can be processed and modelled as a single dataset. Together with Vulcan 2022, the combined grid supports integrated geophysical interpretation of the concealed IOCG system.

collections.title: AusLAMP
collections.description: AusLAMP (Australian Lithospheric Architecture Magnetotelluric Project) is Australia’s  ongoing national long-period magnetotelluric (MT) program. The collection contains  long-period MT surveys acquired across the Australian continent to investigate the electrical resistivity structure of the Australian lithosphere. The resulting models support research into lithospheric architecture, tectonic evolution, crustal and  mantle processes, while providing nationally consistent geophysical data for mineral, groundwater, geothermal, and energy resource exploration. In addition, AusLAMP resistivity models are increasingly used in space weather research, including modelling geomagnetically induced currents (GICs) and assessing the vulnerability of critical  infrastructure to geomagnetic storms. Developed through collaboration between Geoscience Australia, the Australian state and Northern Territory geological surveys, Adelaide University, University of Tasmania and AuScope, AusLAMP provides a nationally consistent MT dataset that supports geoscience research, precompetitive exploration, and the development of models for understanding Australia’s subsurface and its response to space weather.
